claim: RELION-3 includes CPU-based vector acceleration in addition to GPU support.
source: CPU-based vector acceleration has been added in addition to GPU support, which provides flexibility in use of resources and avoids memory limitations.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract of the manuscript.

claim: CPU-based vector acceleration provides flexibility in use of resources and avoids memory limitations.
source: CPU-based vector acceleration has been added in addition to GPU support, which provides flexibility in use of resources and avoids memory limitations.
evidence: This is stated as a benefit of the CPU acceleration in the abstract.

claim: RELION-3 includes reference-free autopicking with Laplacian-of-Gaussian filtering.
source: Reference-free autopicking with Laplacian-of-Gaussian filtering and execution of jobs from python allows non-interactive processing during acquisition, including 2D-classification, de novo model generation and 3D-classification.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a new feature.

claim: RELION-3 allows execution of jobs from python for non-interactive processing during acquisition.
source: Reference-free autopicking with Laplacian-of-Gaussian filtering and execution of jobs from python allows non-interactive processing during acquisition, including 2D-classification, de novo model generation and 3D-classification.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: Per-particle refinement of CTF parameters provides higher resolution reconstructions when particles are at different heights in the ice.
source: Per-particle refinement of CTF parameters and correction of estimated beam tilt provides higher resolution reconstructions when particles are at different heights in the ice, and/or coma-free alignment has not been optimal.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a benefit of the new functionality.

claim: Correction of estimated beam tilt provides higher resolution reconstructions when coma-free alignment has not been optimal.
source: Per-particle refinement of CTF parameters and correction of estimated beam tilt provides higher resolution reconstructions when particles are at different heights in the ice, and/or coma-free alignment has not been optimal.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a benefit of the new functionality.

claim: Ewald sphere curvature correction improves resolution for large particles.
source: Ewald sphere curvature correction improves resolution for large particles.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: RELION-3 leads to resolution improvements of 0.2–0.7 Å compared to previous RELION versions.
source: We illustrate these developments with publicly available data sets: together with a Bayesian approach to beam-induced motion correction it leads to resolution improvements of 0.2–0.7 Å compared to previous RELION versions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data.

claim: Before 2010, cryo-EM structures to resolutions beyond 4 Å had only been obtained for large icosahedral viruses.
source: Before 2010, cryo-EM structures to resolutions beyond 4 Å had only been obtained for large icosahedral viruses, for example Jiang et al., 2008, Yu et al., 2008, and Zhang et al., 2008.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cryo-EM structures to resolutions sufficient for de novo atomic modelling have been achieved for a wide range of samples since 2010.
source: Since then, cryo-EM structures to resolutions that are sufficient for de novo atomic modelling have been achieved for a wide range of samples (Fernandez-Leiro and Scheres, 2016), and several structures beyond 2 Å resolution have been reported (Merk et al., 2016; Bartesaghi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Several cryo-EM structures beyond 2 Å resolution have been reported.
source: Since then, cryo-EM structures to resolutions that are sufficient for de novo atomic modelling have been achieved for a wide range of samples (Fernandez-Leiro and Scheres, 2016), and several structures beyond 2 Å resolution have been reported (Merk et al., 2016; Bartesaghi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The availability of the first prototypes of direct electron detectors in 2012 represented a crucial step forward in cryo-EM.
source: In 2012, the availability of the first prototypes of direct electron detectors, which recorded images with unprecedented signal-to-noise ratios (McMullan et al., 2009), represented a crucial step forward.
evidence: This is stated as a historical fact with citation support.

claim: Direct electron detectors recorded images with unprecedented signal-to-noise ratios.
source: In 2012, the availability of the first prototypes of direct electron detectors, which recorded images with unprecedented signal-to-noise ratios (McMullan et al., 2009), represented a crucial step forward.
evidence: This is supported by citation to McMullan et al., 2009.

claim: Improvements in image processing software closely followed and partially overlapped with the introduction of direct electron detectors.
source: This advance was closely followed and partially overlapped with important improvements in image processing software.
evidence: This is stated as a historical observation.

claim: Direct electron detectors and image processing software improvements together led to the 'resolution revolution' in cryo-EM structure determination.
source: Together, they led to what was termed the 'resolution revolution' in cryo-EM structure determination (Kuhlbrandt, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kuhlbrandt, 2014.

claim: RELION introduced an empirical Bayesian approach where optimal Fourier filters for alignment and reconstruction are derived from the data in a fully automated manner.
source: This computer program introduced an empirical Bayesian approach, in which optimal Fourier filters for alignment and reconstruction are derived from the data in a fully automated manner (Scheres, 2012a).
evidence: This is stated as a feature of RELION with citation support.

claim: RELION's Bayesian approach strongly reduced the need for user expertise in tuning ad-hoc filter parameters compared to existing programs.
source: This strongly reduced the need for user expertise in tuning ad-hoc filter parameters compared to existing programs, and probably contributed to the rapid uptake of cryo-EM structure determination by non-expert groups.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about the impact of RELION's approach.

claim: RELION is widely used.
source: Nowadays, RELION is widely used (Patwardhan, 2017), and similar statistical approaches have been implemented in software packages that were developed since: cryoSPARC (Punjani et al., 2017) uses the same regularised likelihood optimisation target as RELION, and SPHIRE (Moriya et al., 2017) and cisTEM (Grant et al., 2018) implement likelihood-based classification methods.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Patwardhan, 2017.

claim: cryoSPARC uses the same regularised likelihood optimisation target as RELION.
source: Nowadays, RELION is widely used (Patwardhan, 2017), and similar statistical approaches have been implemented in software packages that were developed since: cryoSPARC (Punjani et al., 2017) uses the same regularised likelihood optimisation target as RELION, and SPHIRE (Moriya et al., 2017) and cisTEM (Grant et al., 2018) implement likelihood-based classification methods.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: SPHIRE and cisTEM implement likelihood-based classification methods.
source: Nowadays, RELION is widely used (Patwardhan, 2017), and similar statistical approaches have been implemented in software packages that were developed since: cryoSPARC (Punjani et al., 2017) uses the same regularised likelihood optimisation target as RELION, and SPHIRE (Moriya et al., 2017) and cisTEM (Grant et al., 2018) implement likelihood-based classification methods.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: RELION-2 comprised a pipelined approach for the entire single-particle workflow.
source: RELION underwent a major change in 2016 with the release of its second version, which comprised a pipelined approach for the entire single-particle workflow (Fernandez-Leiro and Scheres, 2016) and used acceleration on graphical procesing units (GPUs) to reduce its computational costs (Kimanius et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: RELION-2 used GPU acceleration to reduce computational costs.
source: RELION underwent a major change in 2016 with the release of its second version, which comprised a pipelined approach for the entire single-particle workflow (Fernandez-Leiro and Scheres, 2016) and used acceleration on graphical procesing units (GPUs) to reduce its computational costs (Kimanius et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: RELION-2's functionality was expanded with the incorporation of sub-tomogram averaging and helical reconstruction.
source: In addition, its functionality was expanded with the incorporation of sub-tomogram averaging (Bharat et al., 2015) and helical reconstruction (He and Scheres, 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The Laplacian-of-Gaussian auto-picking method in RELION-3 is related to the approach in DoGpicker.
source: Our method is related to the approach in DoGpicker (Voss et al., 2009), which uses a Difference-of-Gaussian (DoG) filter.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: CTF refinement in RELION-3 allows CTF estimation to exploit both the phases and the amplitudes of the experimental images.
source: This allows CTF estimation to exploit both the phases and the amplitudes of the experimental images, instead of having to rely exclusively on their power spectra.
evidence: This is stated as a feature of the CTF refinement method.

claim: CTF refinement produces significantly more reliable estimates due to higher signal-to-noise ratios.
source: This approach thus produces significantly more reliable estimates, due to higher signal-to-noise ratios and also because it does not require separation of the Thon rings from the background intensity of the power spectrum.
evidence: This is stated as a benefit of the CTF refinement approach.

claim: The increased stability of CTF fitting can be leveraged to estimate independent defoci for individual particles.
source: The increased stability of the CTF fitting can be leveraged to estimate independent defoci for individual particles.
evidence: This is stated as a capability enabled by the improved CTF fitting.

claim: Similar CTF refinement functionality exists in Frealign and cisTEM.
source: Similar functionality also exists in Frealign (Grigorieff, 2007) and cisTEM (Grant et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The sum over the real components of V*X offers a higher signal-to-noise ratio than power spectra for CTF estimation.
source: Note that the latter term is not only centered around zero, obviating the need to estimate the background intensity, but it also offers a higher signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: A tilted beam alters the phase delays of the scattered beam components with respect to the unscattered reference beam.
source: A tilted beam alters the phase delays of the scattered beam components with respect to the unscattered reference beam.
evidence: This is stated as a physical principle.

claim: RELION-3 implemented the single-side band algorithm to correct for Ewald sphere curvature as proposed by Russo and Henderson, 2018.
source: We implemented the single-side band algorithm to correct for Ewald sphere curvature as proposed by (Russo and Henderson, 2018), which bears resemblance to the method implemented in Frealign (Grigorieff, 2007; Wolf et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The Ewald sphere correction method in RELION-3 bears resemblance to the method implemented in Frealign.
source: We implemented the single-side band algorithm to correct for Ewald sphere curvature as proposed by (Russo and Henderson, 2018), which bears resemblance to the method implemented in Frealign (Grigorieff, 2007; Wolf et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The new CPU code path in RELION-3 uses single precision in most places, which cuts the memory footprint in half.
source: First, the algorithm strength reductions first introduced for the GPU code makes it possible to use single precision in most places, which cuts the memory footprint in half for large parts of the code.
evidence: This is stated as a benefit of the new CPU code path.

claim: The new CPU code in RELION-3 makes use of coalesced memory allocation limited to the orientations that will be investigated.
source: The legacy CPU code would for instance allocate space for all possible orientations under the current sampling level, while the new CPU code makes use of coalesced memory allocation limited to the orientations that will be investigated.
evidence: This is stated as an improvement in the new CPU code.

claim: The standard 3D benchmark runs 1.5x faster on Broadwell processors with the new CPU code compared to legacy code.
source: The standard 3D benchmark for example runs 1.5x and 2.5x faster on the previous (Broadwell) and current (Skylake) generations of x86 processors, respectively (Figure 2A,B), without compromising the results (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The standard 3D benchmark runs 2.5x faster on Skylake processors with the new CPU code compared to legacy code.
source: The standard 3D benchmark for example runs 1.5x and 2.5x faster on the previous (Broadwell) and current (Skylake) generations of x86 processors, respectively (Figure 2A,B), without compromising the results (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Explicitly instructing the compiler to use avx-instructions yields a further performance increase of 5.4x on Skylake-generation CPUs.
source: By explicitly instructing the compiler to use avx-instructions for the new generalised code path, we see a further performance increase of 5.4x on Skylake-generation CPUs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2.

claim: x86 CPU nodes with accelerated code approach the cost-efficiency of professional GPU hardware.
source: This enables x86 CPU nodes to approach the cost-efficiency of professional GPU hardware (Figure 2C), with results that are qualitatively identical to the legacy code path (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The quality of results has not been compromised from using lower precision or compiler optimisation in the new CPU code.
source: The standard 3D benchmark for example runs 1.5x and 2.5x faster on the previous (Broadwell) and current (Skylake) generations of x86 processors, respectively (Figure 2A,B), without compromising the results (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Per-particle defocus variations within a micrograph arise from different particles being situated at different heights within the field of view.
source: Per-particle defocus variations within a micrograph arise from different particles being situated at different heights within the field of view.
evidence: This is stated as a physical explanation.

claim: The influenza virus hemagglutinin dataset (EMPIAR-10097) was collected at 40 degree stage tilt to overcome a strong preferred orientation of the particles.
source: As an extreme case of non-horizontal samples, we re-processed an influenza virus hemagglutinin dataset (EMPIAR-10097) that was collected at 40 degree stage tilt to overcome a strong preferred orientation of the particles (Tan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: At 40 degree tilt angle, the height differences within a single micrograph are more than 4000 Å.
source: At this tilt angle, the height differences within a single micrograph are more than 4000 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the tilt angle.

claim: The influenza virus hemagglutinin dataset was originally published at 4.2 Å resolution.
source: A reconstruction from this data set was originally published at 4.2 Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated as a historical fact.

claim: The influenza virus hemagglutinin data were re-processed in Warp and cryoSPARC, resulting in an improved resolution of 3.2 Å.
source: Recently, the same data were also re-processed in Warp and cryoSPARC, resulting in an improved resolution of 3.2 Å (Tegunov and Cramer, 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: RELION-3 processing of the influenza hemagglutinin dataset yielded a final resolution of 3.1 Å.
source: CTF refinement with beam-tilt correction and 3D refinement were then again iterated three times, giving 3.3 Å, 3.2 Å, and finally 3.1 Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Plots of the final defocus values for particles within a single micrograph clearly replicate the tilt geometry of the experiment.
source: Plots of the final defocus values for particles within a single micrograph clearly replicate the tilt geometry of the experiment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Per-particle defocus refinement in RELION-3 can yield improved defoci even for models with intermediate resolution (6.6 Å).
source: This example demonstrates that even for models with intermediate resolution (in this case 6.6 Å) our per-particle defocus refinement can yield improved defoci.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the influenza hemagglutinin example.

claim: The method for per-particle defocus refinement is robust against the initial values being far off.
source: It also illustrates the robustness of the method against the initial values being far off.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the influenza hemagglutinin example.

claim: Beam tilt has been largely ignored in cryo-EM single-particle analysis until recently.
source: Until to date, beam tilt has been largely ignored in cryo-EM single-particle analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a historical observation.

claim: Currently available microscope alignment procedures may still leave up to a quarter mrad of beam tilt in the data.
source: Based on our experience, we estimate that currently available microscope alignment procedures may still leave up to a quarter mrad of beam tilt in the data.
evidence: This is stated as an estimate based on experience.

claim: Beam-shift is faster than physically moving the sample stage.
source: Because it is much faster to shift the electron beam instead, one could achieve higher data acquisition rates by using beam-shift to image multiple holes before shifting the stage.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for using beam-shift.

claim: Beam-shift introduces beam tilt.
source: Beam-shift is already used extensively to take multiple images within a single hole, but because it introduces beam tilt, its use for imaging multiple holes has only recently attracted attention (Cheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The first ferritin data set with active beam tilt compensation yielded a resolution of 2.3 Å after standard 3D auto-refinement.
source: The first data set, with active beam tilt compensation, yielded a resolution of 2.3 Å after standard 3D auto-refinement, and 2.2 Å after Bayesian polishing and a second round of refinement (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The second ferritin data set without active beam tilt compensation yielded 2.9 Å after the first refinement.
source: The second data set, without active beam tilt compensation, yielded 2.9 Å after the first refinement, and 2.8 Å after Bayesian polishing.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Beam tilt correction improved the resolution of the second ferritin data set to 2.2 Å.
source: A third round of refinement with correction for the estimated beam tilts improved the resolution to 2.2 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Beam tilt estimation and correction in RELION-3 may be a feasible alternative to active beam tilt compensation at the microscope.
source: These results illustrate that beam tilt estimation and correction in RELION-3 may be a feasible alternative to active beam tilt compensation at the microscope.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the ferritin beam tilt experiments.

claim: The P22 virion capsid protein has a diameter of approximately 700 Å.
source: The diameter of the P22 virion is approximately 700 Å, which leads to an estimated resolution limit of 3.1 Å due to Ewald sphere curvature (DeRosier, 2000).
evidence: This is stated as a property of the P22 virion.

claim: The estimated resolution limit for P22 virion due to Ewald sphere curvature is 3.1 Å.
source: The diameter of the P22 virion is approximately 700 Å, which leads to an estimated resolution limit of 3.1 Å due to Ewald sphere curvature (DeRosier, 2000).
evidence: This is stated with citation to DeRosier, 2000.

claim: Standard 3D auto-refinement of P22 virion data gave a reconstruction with an estimated resolution of 3.5 Å.
source: Standard 3D auto-refinement, with correction for an estimated beam tilt of 0.6 mrad in X and −0.13 mrad in Y, gave a reconstruction with an estimated resolution of 3.5 Å (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Ewald sphere correction improved the P22 virion reconstruction to 3.3 Å.
source: Subsequent Ewald sphere correction improved this to 3.3 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Ewald sphere correction with the opposite curvature gave only 3.9 Å for P22 virion.
source: Ewald sphere correction with the opposite curvature gave only 3.9 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Ewald sphere correction could be used to determine the absolute hand of a structure if the number of mirroring operations is known.
source: In theory, if one knows the number of mirroring operations during data acquisition and image processing, Ewald sphere correction could therefore also be used to determine the absolute hand of a structure.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical possibility.

claim: At the resolutions where Ewald sphere correction matters, determining absolute hand is often no longer a relevant question.
source: However, at the resolutions where Ewald sphere correction matters, this is often no longer a relevant question.
evidence: This is stated as a practical observation.

claim: The final resolution for the γ-secretase dataset processed with RELION-3 was 3.3 Å.
source: A second 3D classification yielded a majority class with 240,777 particles, which led to a final resolution of 3.3 Å (Figure 6E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The original processing of the γ-secretase dataset in RELION-1.3 obtained a map at 3.4 Å resolution from 159,549 particles.
source: When we originally processed this data set in RELION-1.3, we obtained a map at 3.4 Å resolution from 159,549 particles, which were selected after 3D classification of 412,272 polished particles (Bai et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Processing the same set of 412,272 γ-secretase particles with RELION-3 gave a final resolution of 3.2 Å.
source: To assess whether the non-interactive pre-processing procedure can compete with this expert-driven approach, we used the same set of 412,272 particles also for Bayesian polishing, refinement of per-particle defocus values, beam tilt estimation and 3D classification. The resulting selection of 246,602 particles gave a final resolution of 3.2 Å (Figure 6E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6.

claim: The improvement from 3.4 Å to 3.2 Å for γ-secretase represents the contribution of the new functionality in RELION-3.
source: The improvement from 3.4 Å to 3.2 Å represents the contribution of the new functionality in RELION-3, whereas the gain from 3.3 Å to 3.2 Å represents the added value of the expert user.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: The gain from 3.3 Å to 3.2 Å for γ-secretase represents the added value of the expert user.
source: The improvement from 3.4 Å to 3.2 Å represents the contribution of the new functionality in RELION-3, whereas the gain from 3.3 Å to 3.2 Å represents the added value of the expert user.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: The map from the automatically pre-processed γ-secretase data does not correlate with the atomic model as well as one would expect from the half-map FSC curves.
source: However, the map from the automatically pre-processed data does not correlate with the atomic model as well as one would expect from the half-map FSC curves.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the results.

claim: The lower correlation of the automatically pre-processed γ-secretase map suggests a higher fraction of false positives compared to the expert selection.
source: This suggests a higher fraction of false positives in the data resulting from the relion_it.py script compared to the expert selection, which may be caused by the relatively low default for the auto-picking threshold in the script.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observation.

claim: Non-interactive pre-processing gets close to the performance of a human expert for γ-secretase.
source: These results illustrate that non-interactive pre-processing gets close to the performance of a human expert, but for challenging data sets there is still a benefit in careful tuning of parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the γ-secretase example.

claim: For challenging data sets there is still a benefit in careful tuning of parameters compared to non-interactive pre-processing.
source: These results illustrate that non-interactive pre-processing gets close to the performance of a human expert, but for challenging data sets there is still a benefit in careful tuning of parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the γ-secretase example.

claim: Using RELION-2.0, a 2.2 Å resolution reconstruction (EMD-4116) was previously obtained for the β-galactosidase data set at EMPIAR-10061.
source: This data set was made available to the community by the Subramaniam group. Using RELION-2.0, we previously obtained a 2.2 Å resolution reconstruction (EMD-4116).
evidence: This is stated as a historical result.

claim: An initial 3D auto-refinement of β-galactosidase yielded a map with an estimated resolution of 2.3 Å.
source: An initial 3D auto-refinement with these particles yielded a map with an estimated resolution of 2.3 Å (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Re-refining β-galactosidase after only per-particle defocus refinement improved the resolution to 2.2 Å.
source: Re-refining the same data set after only per-particle defocus refinement or beam tilt estimation improved the resolution to 2.2 in both cases.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Re-refining β-galactosidase after only beam tilt estimation improved the resolution to 2.2 Å.
source: Re-refining the same data set after only per-particle defocus refinement or beam tilt estimation improved the resolution to 2.2 in both cases.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Application of both per-particle defocus refinement and beam tilt estimation gave 2.1 Å resolution for β-galactosidase.
source: Application of both methods gave 2.1 Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Bayesian polishing of β-galactosidase gave 1.94 Å resolution.
source: We then performed Bayesian polishing, which gave 1.94 Å, and classified the resulting shiny particles into six classes.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: The final resolution for β-galactosidase after all processing steps in RELION-3 was 1.90 Å.
source: A second round of per-particle defocus refinement and beam tilt estimation, followed by another 3D auto-refinement yielded a final resolution of 1.90 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: Ewald sphere correction for the β-galactosidase data set did not improve the resolution by at least one Fourier shell.
source: Ewald sphere correction for this data set did not improve the resolution by at least one Fourier shell, although a small increase in FSC values near the estimated resolution was visible.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: The bfactor_plot.py script produced an estimate for the overall B-factor of 56 Å² for β-galactosidase.
source: Application of the bfactor_plot.py script produced an estimate for the overall B-factor of 56 Å2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The bfactor_plot.py script predicts a resolution of 1.75 Å for β-galactosidase when using four times more particles.
source: By extrapolation, the script predicts a resolution of 1.75 Å when using four times more particles, and 1.69 Å when using eight times more particles.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the script.

claim: The bfactor_plot.py script predicts a resolution of 1.69 Å for β-galactosidase when using eight times more particles.
source: By extrapolation, the script predicts a resolution of 1.75 Å when using four times more particles, and 1.69 Å when using eight times more particles.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the script.

claim: The Subramaniam group re-processed the β-galactosidase data set using new methods, resulting in map EMD-7770 with a reported resolution of 1.9 Å.
source: Recently, the Subramaniam group also re-processed this data set using new methods for defocus estimation, motion correction and radiation damage weighting (Bartesaghi et al., 2018). The resulting map (EMD-7770) was reported as an atomic resolution structure. The resolution according to the 0.143 FSC criterion was 1.9 Å.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The RELION-3 β-galactosidase map correlated with PDB-5A1A to 0.15 Å higher resolution than EMD-7770.
source: Despite the same nominal resolution of 1.9 Å, the RELION-3 map correlated with PDB-5A1A to 0.15 Å higher resolution than EMD-7770 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: FSC curves provide an objective overall assessment of map quality when suitably soft and low-resolution masks are used and care is taken to avoid overfitting.
source: Nevertheless, provided suitably soft and low-resolution masks are used and care is taken to avoid overfitting (Scheres and Chen, 2012; Brown et al., 2015), FSC curves provide an objective overall assessment of map quality.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The human apo-ferritin data were collected on the same K2 detector and Titan Krios microscope as the horse spleen apo-ferritin data set.
source: For a final illustration of the combined functionality in RELION-3, we processed a data set on a human apo-ferritin sample, which was a gift from Fei Sun. These data were collected on the same K2 detector and Titan Krios microscope as the horse spleen apo-ferritin data set in section 3.3.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the data collection.

claim: The human apo-ferritin data have been deposited at EMPIAR-10200.
source: We have deposited these data at EMPIAR-10200.
evidence: This is stated as a data availability statement.

claim: A final 3D refinement of human apo-ferritin yielded a resolution of 1.65 Å.
source: Selection of suitable 2D class averages led to a subset of 426,450 particles, which were subjected to Bayesian polishing and per-particle defocus refinement. A final 3D refinement yielded a resolution of 1.65 Å, which is two resolution shells below the Nyquist frequency (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8.

claim: The 1.65 Å resolution for human apo-ferritin is two resolution shells below the Nyquist frequency.
source: A final 3D refinement yielded a resolution of 1.65 Å, which is two resolution shells below the Nyquist frequency (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a property of the resolution.

claim: Estimation of the beam tilt for human apo-ferritin yielded values below 0.1 mrad.
source: Estimation of the beam tilt yielded values below 0.1 mrad, and refinement with these values did not improve the map.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the processing.

claim: The human apo-ferritin map shows spherical-like features around some of the atoms.
source: As expected at this resolution, the map shows spherical-like features around some of the atoms (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The bfactor_plot.py script produced an estimate for the overall B-factor of 66 Å² for human apo-ferritin.
source: Application of the bfactor_plot.py script produced an estimate for the overall B-factor of 66 Å2﻿ (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Completely automated, high-resolution cryo-EM structure determination of relatively straightforward samples like apo-ferritin is within close reach.
source: Thereby, completely automated, high-resolution cryo-EM structure determination of relatively straightforward samples like apo-ferritin is within close reach.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the apo-ferritin example.

claim: The new functionality in RELION-3 allows faster, more automated and higher resolution cryo-EM structure determination compared to previous versions.
source: The new functionality in RELION-3 allows faster, more automated and higher resolution cryo-EM structure determination compared to previous versions.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion.

claim: CPU acceleration makes it possible to use a much wider range of hardware efficiently for RELION.
source: CPU acceleration makes it possible to use a much wider range of hardware efficiently for RELION, including laptops and desktops, and it avoids the box size limits still present when offloading to GPU accelerators.
